adaptations: References relocated into the two-folder package.
Established input, roster, tool inventory, date, reporting and static-injection overrides applied.
Repeated instructions use the numbered Eval instead of copying entire guides.
External sample folders are not required; supplied samples may be compared optionally.
Scored labels and numerical thresholds retained; current numbered-Eval overrides still govern.
Direct-search variant: source reads use the selected local archive; original scoring thresholds and persona/ACL policy are unchanged.
Issued verdicts are always PASS/NON-FAIL/FAIL; unresolved required evidence without a proven failure uses provisional NON-FAIL and PARTIAL/BLOCKED. Existing numerical thresholds are unchanged.

injection-static-v2 supersedes prior injection quality/difficulty rules: only records/IDs, SQL structure under available supported definitions, and data consistency are required. Runtime compatibility is disclosed, not certified. Removed injection style, reply-pairing, discovery and difficulty gates; other stage scoring definitions retained.

stage-evidence-v1: explicit stage ownership, reuse of supported unchanged source/check evidence with matching dependencies, prompt-only interpretation without later golden/rubric/run inputs, prompt design gates separate from observed hardness, and artifact-specific golden/rubric/hint checks. Numeric thresholds and scored JSON definitions retained; auditor guidance updated.
User-approved relative-date policy: contextual Friday/today/yesterday wording is allowed; only material ambiguity or temporal contradiction is a defect. Fixed universe clock retained.

prompt-incorporation-v1 supersedes the former company-policy exception: requirements come only from the prompt and instructions it clearly incorporates. Unmentioned handbook/onboarding/policy records add no obligations even when official or injected; discovered facts remain usable. Trace each instruction to its prompt passage, exclude hidden-rule criteria and difficulty misses, and reassess older requirement maps before reuse. Existing persona/ACL, capabilities, score thresholds and output paths remain unchanged.

Output-capability safeguard: verify creation, real format generation/export and delivery using the task Agent's supported tool/runtime path. Confirmed absence is a task/environment defect, not an Agent failure; unknown support remains unresolved. Generic MIME/extension fields and evaluator-local tools do not prove capability. Existing verdict vocabulary and numeric scoring rules retained.

model-aware-v3: Opus-first selection remains unchanged. Assess Opus directly; for Haiku fallback predict Opus difficulty with the active Evals/1B_Haiku_Prediction_Eval.md transfer and cohort-sweep screen. Record actual run model and separate assessment mode. Haiku severity alone never establishes Opus difficulty; qualifying prediction uses PREDICTED_OPUS_DIFFICULTY, not observed-model failure. No backfill, golden, rubric or calibration batch is required. Disclose qualitative uncertainty without numerical pass-rate forecasts. Preserve evidence sufficiency, fixed report paths and other stage rules. A matching Opus backfill replaces the prediction with direct observation.

hardness-eval-split-v1: /hardness identifies the selected run model before loading rules. Opus reads only Evals/1A_Hardness_Eval.md; Haiku reads only Evals/1B_Haiku_Prediction_Eval.md. Haiku prediction mechanics moved out of shared/Opus reads. Existing model-aware-v3 scoring, intake selection and report contracts are unchanged; this adds no command or report stage.

rubric-consistent-v1: organize six review checks and add explicit contradiction detection with time/scope/conditional guards. Remove conflicting companion-criterion and prohibition exceptions, distinguish unverified from demonstrated wrong evidence, align create/audit Process at the existing 40% cap, and separate six scored dimensions from supporting gates. Keep percentage thresholds, five-field export, 1/3/5 weights, source authority, Split Completely and output paths. Conditional AF scoring without runs is N/A, not an observed 5; the existing static 2+ invalid-AF gate needs proven defects. Consolidate repeated checklists and reporting ledgers.

rubric-consistent-v2: build source-backed acceptance predicates before authoring and record per-row valid alternatives and near misses; distinguish scoped metrics from independent reported results; allow explicit objective eligibility rules; resolve affected work by branch and property; remove contradictory duplicate and whole-column examples. Keep verdict bands, numeric thresholds, export schema, weights, optional Process policy and deterministic output paths. Readiness is a separate report field, not a new verdict or JSON field.

rubric-revision-v3 supersedes the create-mode procedure in rubric-consistent-v2: stage a five-field JSON proposal, evaluate every acceptance predicate with a valid-solution challenge and a plausible wrong-result challenge, automatically repair demonstrated defects and reevaluate until supported PASS. Only the exact current proposal with a matching COMPLETE CREATE PASS (5), zero open substantive defects and unresolved checks can publish to Evals/task_inputs/5_Rubric.json. Drafts, review context and prior generated output are archived; changed task grounding invalidates old prefill. Audit-only inputs/reviews preserve supplied criteria and existing exports. Preserve six numeric dimensions, score thresholds, 1/3/5 weights, optional Process policy, authority/capability rules and fixed paths; readiness enforcement does not independently grade semantics.

historical-injection-dates-v1: injected records may predate January 1, 2026, including newly inserted or updated historical records. Remove the global earliest-date cutoff from injection/golden evals and shared scoring. Keep the universe clock at 2026-02-14 00:00 without a timezone and verify actual chronology, relationships and task-specific date scope. Future scheduled events may be represented as future; completed events must fit the clock. Prior January-cutoff findings require reassessment under this rule, not automatic relabeling of historical reports.

golden-audit-v1: audit the whole supplied golden with six evidence-based checks for worked-solution completeness, factual accuracy, requirement authority, valid-solution acceptance, wrong-solution rejection, and consistency/feasibility. Preserve input bytes; report exact passages, source/requirement mappings, counterexamples and specific corrections. Distinguish example choices from mandatory conditions and intended solver outputs from the golden prose; accept supported open-ended alternatives without importing rubric atomicity or layout rules. Missing citations and reviewer evidence are not automatic factual failures. Preserve PASS (5)/COMPLETE, demonstrated FAIL without score, provisional NON-FAIL/PARTIAL or BLOCKED without score, current inputs, no-rubric/no-routine-run scope, fixed clock, historical injection allowance and report path. This changes audit instructions, not the default command mode or golden publication behavior.

ruthless-grading-v1: all six commands and both hardness branches apply one shared evidence-based tough-grading standard. Actively challenge acceptance and score rationales, complete applicable checks, substantiate findings and preserve supported valid alternatives. No automatic failures from missing reviewer evidence, no added hidden constraints, no inflated severity or failure-rate targets. Existing stage gates, numeric thresholds, verdict meanings, inputs, audit/create modes, evidence reuse and deterministic paths remain unchanged.

horizon-tiers-v1: user correction on 2026-09-18 sets Super Long Horizon to 500+ necessary task-Agent calls, with no 1,000-call cap; Long Horizon retains its 100-call starting point and covers 100–499 calls. Supersedes the former 500–1,000 Long Horizon rule and archived taxonomy 1,000+ Super Long starting point. Normal Horizon guidance is unchanged. Assess prompt design without requesting a trajectory, distinguish estimates from observations, use efficient supported tool paths, and never infer difficulty or quality from volume alone. The Haiku cohort-sweep route uses the applicable tier. Reassess stale boundary-based findings before reuse; historical reports/calibration remain historical.

rubric-revision-v4 retains the v3 generation/revision loop and audit scoring. CREATE publication additionally requires a structured review record binding every current row, requirement coverage, concrete valid/wrong cases, supporting-field checks, whole-rubric mutations and explicit permitted sampling limits to the proposal and report hashes. Missing records and failed or unresolved declared checks prevent publication. The helper verifies completeness and declarations, not source truth or semantic correctness. Legacy v3 reports remain readable but cannot authorize new publication.

golden-audit-v3 retains the six v1 audit checks and verdict semantics. Every new PASS additionally requires a structured evidence record with source-file hashes, factual claims, source-derived requirement coverage, completed absence/calculation/cohort checks and concrete valid/wrong cases, bound to the exact supplied answer, input/rule context, audit iteration and report. Missing, stale or declared failed/unresolved evidence blocks PASS. The helper validates completeness, references and declared judgments, not semantic truth or omitted requirements. Legacy reports remain readable; demonstrated FAIL and provisional NON-FAIL reports remain savable without fabricated evidence. Default /golden preserves the supplied answer; no generation, automatic repair, publication loop, rubric input or external model run is added. V3 format-2 records anchor exact source and saved-answer passages, explicitly identify persona-visible supporting sources, review source chronology and main/alternative consistency, and verify claimed repairs against the saved answer. Bound reports must agree with the recorded findings; the helper does not establish semantic truth or completeness.

rubric-revision-v6 retains existing audit scores and the proposal/review/revision loop. Format-3 CREATE records inventory independently required entity/property/output outcomes before drafting, bind every row to that inventory, and require concrete independence tests, partial-success witnesses and split plans for bundles. Independent or unresolved results block publication even under contradictory PASS labels. Narrow one-result cases and qualified large-audit controls/spot checks remain valid; no minimum criterion count is introduced. Record validation enforces completeness and consistency, not semantic truth or accurate decomposition. Older v3/v4/v5 reports remain readable but cannot authorize new publication. The final five-field JSON, paths, model setting and other stages are unchanged. V6 verifies exact source quotes and saved-prompt incorporation chains, inventories restrictive clauses, tests every supported golden alternative against the whole rubric, and checks declared outcome ownership for repeated grading. Both audit and create scored reports require a bound rubric-score record computing highest-severity-once fractions, existing thresholds and lowest applicable dimension/gate score; no numeric boundaries change.

rubric-revision-v7: Format-4 CREATE records add a per-row assertion inventory with exact criterion excerpts, roles, actual subjects/properties and existing outcome links. Independently required per-entity statuses split even when expressed as one list or mapped to one ID. Multiple required assertions, grouped per-entity properties, extra requirements in supporting fields and unresolved inventories block publication. Supporting detail needs a successful omission test. Necessary qualifiers, literal identity membership, eligible aggregates and one comparison/conclusion supported by multiple sources remain valid. Source history and unrequested dates do not become new grading requirements. The same semantic review applies in AUDIT. User analytics-event cases plus repaired/valid controls calibrate the boundary; helper checks do not infer missing assertions or prove classifications true. Existing numeric rules, JSON output schema, persona/ACL rules, report paths and model settings remain unchanged; v6 reports remain readable but cannot authorize v7 publication.

rubric-revision-v8 / golden-audit-v4 (2026-09-22): severity is impact-aware (incorrect/unauthorized/non_atomic/overly_broad are Major only when they change acceptance, with a recorded witness); hard gates are derived from recorded issues and tiered catastrophic/localized; uncovered outcomes enter the denominator as virtual rows with criticality; three acceptance-changing rows fail at any percentage; every issue records provenance; platform defects are recorded, not scored; scoring record format 2. Golden intake refuses a 5,000-character cut, a mid-sentence ending or a wrong-task artifact; every value in the golden must be a ledgered claim; failing findings carry defect_class and repair_owner; record format 3; /golden fix repair loop. rubric-draft requires a current golden PASS record and rubric-json never publishes against an unverified golden. coherent_record atomicity exception adopted from the 2026-09-22 consistency trial. Deviates from the QC-spec severity-by-type table by design.

service-availability-v1 (2026-09-23): apply the user-supplied project confirmation that Snowflake and Confluence are live. Remove the retired-server feasibility ban; original ACL omission alone cannot produce FAIL, HOLD, PARTIAL/BLOCKED or forced replacement. Preserve concrete task-specific access checks, seven scoped/four unscoped classifications, capability/data/schema verification, local-only execution and all numeric scoring thresholds. Reassess affected historical findings without automatically changing whole-task verdicts.

service-availability-v1 addendum (2026-09-23): the Prompt/Feasibility 'Notes for Auditors' entry in scoring.json is aligned to the live-service rule (the former 'unverified by that matrix; do not infer scope' sentence is replaced). Scored labels and thresholds are unchanged. The scoring.json manifest hash is refreshed; the prior recorded hash predated the 2026-09-22 rubric-revision-v8 edit.

rubric-revision-v9 (2026-09-23): format-3 scored CREATE and AUDIT records require exact-title, prompt-clause, substantive-outcome and row-assertion checks. Recognized artifact subjects cannot be labelled Agent-centric; declared bundles require atomicity issues/gates; accepted omissions of required outcomes cannot be downgraded to optional depth. Source hashes, partial-success and omission/wrong-result tests are reconciled with issues and coverage. Preserve coherent-record and verified precision-only controls; unresolved evidence stays provisional. Use authored criterion count as denominator, unique missing outcomes in numerator only. Align negative framing with the user-supplied QC exception for explicit prompt/incorporated prohibitions. v8 records remain historical, not current publication authority. Golden-audit-v4, model routing, service-availability-v1 and submitted artifacts are unchanged. These checks do not prove semantic truth.

rubric-revision-v10 (2026-09-24) supersedes v8/v9 rubric scoring and publication policy: QC category severities and authored-row denominator, overlap-group numerator, separate Criteria Weights, no absolute-three-row grade override. Six static dimensions; no verifier/all-failing/batch inputs. Both AUDIT and CREATE require source-bound executable numeric/date/literal facts, source-backed semantic reviews, restrictions and whole-set alternatives. Numeric/title-unit mismatches require Incorrect findings; missing evidence remains unresolved. Score and publication readiness are separate. Preserve golden-audit-v4, models, other-stage scoring and service-availability-v1.

rubric-eval-only-v1: user-approved evaluation-only workflow for /rubric and /rubric audit. Requires supplied criteria, preserves their bytes, reports QC findings and suggested repairs, and stops. CREATE scoring and rubric-draft/rubric-review/rubric-json writer routes are retired; no prefill or automatic repair loop. No golden PASS prerequisite. Internal scoring and evidence binding remain; existing v10 grading thresholds, factual checks, atomicity exceptions and spot-check rules are unchanged. Supersedes prior rubric generation/publication instructions; historical schemas and validation records are not active workflow instructions.

rubric-sampling-v1 (2026-09-25): user-approved coverage clarification. Cover core/distinct outcomes directly; sample repetitive artifact contents of comparable importance using exact scope controls and justified ordinary/edge selections. Conditional sampling groups bind scope evidence, outcomes, protected requirements and limits. Eligible unsampled cells are not fabricated missing outcomes. Every supplied criterion is still reviewed; no fixed row-count trigger, sample quota or criterion cap. Missing reviewer metadata is not a new QC failure. Preserve v10 severities, authored-row denominator, 1/3/5 complexity weights and rubric-eval-only-v1; no rubric rewriting, verifier inputs, second reviewer or model run. Other stages are unchanged.

prompt-rubric-reliability-v1 (2026-09-25): prompt/rubric-only source and release enforcement. Bound prompt premise records distinguish facts from new outputs and hypotheses. Authoring metadata cannot establish factual matches or contradictions. Conditional absence checks require applicable coverage and positive controls. Explicit numerical bands compare unrounded source values. Runtime manifests bind new scored reports; historical versions remain separate. Preserve rubric v10 scoring, 1/3/5 weights, atomicity/sampling exceptions and evaluation-only workflow. Golden, hardness, hint and injection behavior unchanged. Local tests do not prove arbitrary semantic correctness.

oracle-events-v1 (2026-09-25): user-requested replacement of active golden evaluation by /oe. Completeness and Accuracy each score 5 or NON-FAIL 3; no FAIL band. Local summary is the minimum. Full critical path, source/tool/parameter/expected-data accuracy, Outcome-first rubric mapping, separate oe input/report, exact evidence/release binding, and safe managed-skill migration. Historical golden artifacts and helper compatibility remain; rubric stays evaluation-only with unchanged QC bands and sampling.

rubric-category-names-v1 (2026-09-25): use only Outcome and Process in rubric categories, review prose and coverage maps. Remove obsolete numbered category subtypes. Scoring, required outcome coverage, Outcome-first policy and atomicity exceptions are unchanged.

prompt-rubric-qc-examples-v1 (2026-09-25): separate prompt-only and rubric historical examples guide existing evidence and acceptance checks. Preserve 117 flags on 88 dimension-specific cards with exact prompts, rubric rows and explanations; exported labels remain unverified. Challenge material ambiguity, approval/ownership, identity/source conflicts, missing required writes and output content, alternatives and contradictions. Exclude known historical case/guide files from primary factual authority. Preserve prompt pre-run boundaries, rubric v10 scoring, sampling, atomicity exceptions, complexity weights, Outcome-first categories and evaluation-only behavior. No verifier, external model or original-universe replay is introduced.

hg-strict-overrides-v1 (2026-09-26, user-approved): supersedes the QC workbook for rubric review. Overly Specific that rejects a valid answer is Major and harmless specificity Minor; Overly Broad is Moderate; rows that would all fail on one Agent error because each embeds the same acceptance condition form one Moderate overlap group; prohibition-only acceptance fails Negative Criteria even with prompt authority; self-containment is title-only; two or more predicted all-fail rows force FAIL. Categories stay Outcome/Process. Prompt review adds that a leading interpretation alone does not resolve ambiguity and checks task-relevant injected records for duplicates and contradictions.

docs-restructure-v1 (2026-09-26, user-approved): Evals/Docs holds the QC spec, rating form and guidelines as the authority; Evals 1, 2 and 3 follow the original repository layout with a Local Overrides table listing each departure. /hint, Hint Requiredness, the reference-model check and the hinted verifier run are removed. Tool-call counts move to Trajectory - Task Type & Horizon (100% run count, else average of six; Normal 50-100, Long 100-500+); the >15 prompt gate and average-15 floor are removed. Failure patterns need >=2 patterns differing on >=2 rubric results. Category Balance fails only at zero Outcome. OE verdicts follow the Oracle Events guideline: missing or wrong step FAIL 2; minor, non-action, final-response NON-FAIL 3. Prompt: competency/task skill and date contradictions stay FAIL, feasibility has no middle band, tool mention is pass/fail, universe coherence follows the QC form, AI-text and opaque-ID checks added, relative dates allowed. Clock 2026-02-14 00:00 UTC.

prompt-ugt-v1: format-2 prompt records require a source-bound two-reading comparison before any scored Unique Ground Truth verdict, including PASS within an overall FAIL or partial report. Account for every explicit option, challenge alternative strength and actual resolving authority, and bind the generated comparison to the saved report. Preserve unscored incomplete reviews and PASS 5 / FAIL 1-2 UGT bands; no semantic guarantee is inferred from structural validation.

User-approved UGT five-check clarification: newer applicable source, authority, source identity, scope and same material result. Later same-issue updates can resolve conflicts without explicit replacement language, subject to task cutoff and source priority; partial updates retain unaffected requirements. The mandatory two-reading comparison, all-option review, scored bands and existing evidence-record format remain in force.

Historical reference only; not an active scoring dependency.

historical_adaptations: observed-run-v5: mandatory Haiku hardness gate for Opus average weighted pass rate below 75%; consequential retrieval, reconciliation, synthesis and reuse/exclusion failures can qualify. Bundled empirical comparisons guide the screen without numeric forecasts, imported weights or automatic promotion. Existing score bands retained; HOLD blocks Opus and dependent authoring.

observed-run-v6: supersedes v5's promotion test with a fourth thorough-reader counterfactual check. Each candidate chain records transfer_class; a chain whose decisive step is an unissued search, an unopened pointer, an unread returned record or a rule stated verbatim in a source the run already held is CAPABILITY_FLOOR and cannot qualify, however consequential it was in that run. Only JUDGMENT_AMBIGUITY chains support 3-5; 3 versus 4 turns on independent root causes rather than chain count; decision_rule_source caps enumerated_single_source tasks at 2 without a judgment chain. An all-CAPABILITY_FLOOR screen is scored low difficulty, not insufficient evidence. Pattern IDs describe evidence shape and never establish transfer. Existing score bands, gate reasons and the below-75% target retained; v5 PROCEED verdicts require reassessment. hardness_calibration.md records paired outcomes for rule review only and never scores a task under review.

observed-run-v7: supersedes v6 by adding the cohort-sweep route. v6's counterfactual assumes complete retrieval, so it cannot judge a task where the sweep is the work, and its observed-failure requirement cannot be met when the screening model abandons a large inventory early. A SCALE_COMPLETENESS chain may qualify only when the golden requires record-level evidence across a source-defined cohort in the long-horizon band, no bulk call holds that evidence, the deliverable carries exact totals derived per record, and applying the predicate to one record is more than a lookup. scale_evidence records paired_runs or design_only; the latter advances a task provisionally as DESIGN_SCALE_UNPAIRED. decision_rule_source now yields to a credited sweep chain. Volume, row count, clause count, service count and tool-call count still establish nothing on their own. v6 HOLD verdicts on cohort-sweep tasks require reassessment.

opus-run-v1 supersedes the Haiku screen: one unhinted Opus run is assessed directly for observed correctness, usability and delivery. Retrieval, rule-following and execution failures count by impact. Task/environment defects are excluded. No cross-model transfer tests, counterfactual reader, source-shape cap, calibration or design-only advancement. Scored reviews require COMPLETE; insufficient evidence is unscored provisional NON-FAIL with HOLD. HOLD never prevents obtaining a run for assessment. One run cannot establish an average below 75%.

direct-run-v2: prefer one unhinted Opus run and support an existing Haiku run when Opus is unavailable. Assess either model directly with the same ordinal bands and model-specific gate reasons; a supported Haiku fallback can proceed without Opus backfill, but establishes no Opus difficulty claim. Explicit selection wins; otherwise use Opus first. Preserve separate model slots and raw exports, resolve damaged preferred inputs instead of silently downgrading, confirm model and task/source match, and record Assessed model on every report. A later matching Opus run is assessed afresh. No cross-model prediction or retired transfer rules return.

SUPERSEDED by prompt-incorporation-v1; not active guidance: User-approved task requirement authority: valid prompt incorporation or authoritative company-wide onboarding/handbook/general policy that is applicable, Agent-accessible and current. Inspect optional SQL and relevant sources, document source-to-requirement-to-criterion coverage, and preserve task-specific prompt-reference requirements. Injection/title alone never confers authority; scoring thresholds unchanged.
